uncited: Neural Network Parameter Quantization reduces the memory footprint and bandwidth requirements of neural volume representations (such as Neural Radiance Fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting) by mapping continuous network weights or feature values to discrete, lower-bit representations.
It solves the problem of high VRAM consumption and slow training/inference caused by storing full-precision floating-point parameters for large-scale neural fields.
The family shares the fundamental mechanism of mapping a continuous input space to a discrete output space.

While specific implementations vary, the core operation involves a quantization function $Q(x)$ that maps a real-valued input $x$ to a discrete index or representative value, and an inverse function for reconstruction.
**Discretization:** Continuous values (voxel intensities, transform coefficients, neural network weights, or color components) are mapped to a finite set of levels.
**Indexing/Representation:** The quantized data is represented by compact indices, bit-packed integers, or reduced-precision floating-point formats .
